COMPACTNESS               IN T H E      LATTICE          OF    SUBGROUPS
OF     A TOPOLOGICAL                GROUP

          Yu.    A.   Komarov         and    I.   V.    Protasov                                                             UDC 519.46


          The study of topological groups with r e s p e c t to the p r o p e r t i e s of s y s t e m s of t h e i r closed subgroups is one
of the main directions of the algebraic theory of topological groups. In this connection, as the defining r e s t r i c -
tions, as a rule we choose suitable analogs of r e s t r i c t i o n s f r o m the domain of d i s c r e t e groups. Basing on the
topology of a group G, we can introduce a topology in the lattice ~ (G) of its closed subgroups, which, in its
t u r n , opens up new possibilities for the study of groups with r e s p e c t to the p r o p e r t i e s of the topologized s y s -
tems of their closed subgroups. Since even in the case of a discrete group G the topology in ~ (6)" is, in gen-
e r a l , nontrivial, in this way there a r i s e new results in the theory of discrete groups also.
       Let G be a topological group, ~e (6) be the lattice of its closed subgroups that is equipped with the E -
topology (see [1]). The s t r u c t u r e of locally compact groups with a compact lattice ~e (6) (the EK-groups) has
been studied m [1]. Let us denote the families of the monothetic, the Abelian, and the n o r m a l subgroups f r o m
~e (6) by 9~ (6), ~ (6), and 9} (6) , r e s p e c t i v e l y , and the families of the compact and the noncompact subgroups
from ~e (6) by ~ (6} and n~ (6), r e s p e c t i v e l y .
      We retain the t e r m i n o l o g y and the notation of [1]; in p a r t i c u l a r , in the sequel only closed subgroups of a
topological group will be cMied its subgroups. All the c o n s i d e r e d topological groups, unless stated otherwise,
are supposed to be locally compact.

         COROLLARY 2.          If G is locally compact and ~(G) is compact in the E-topology, then G is compact.
        Proof. It follows f r o m T h e o r e m 1 that ~e (6) is compact. If G is not compact, then by L e m m a 10 of [1]

      COROLLARY 3. If G is a totally disconnected locally compact group, then ~ ( 6 ) is compact in the E -
topology if and only if G is compact.
          Proof. Compactness of G under the condition of c o m p a c t n e s s of ~(G) follows f r o m C o r o l l a r y 2. The
converse follows f r o m the fact that if a net {x~}, ~ E J, of elements of a totally disconnected c o m p a c t group
converges to x, then the net of subgroups {<xc~}}, c~ E J , converges in the E-topology to <x} (see the proof of
T h e o r e m 1 in [3]).
      R e m a r k 2. In general, c o m p a c t n e s s of G does not imply c o m p a c t n e s s of ~0~ (6). As an example, we can
take an a r b i t r a r y connected compact Abelian group of weight g r e a t e r than the cardinality of the continuum.
        A topological group G is said to be c r a m p e d (see [4]) if each subset of pairwise noncomparable subgroups
f r o m ~ (G)' is finite.
         THEOREM 2.          The lattice ge (6) of each compactly coverable c r a m p e d group G is compact.
        Proof. By virtue of T h e o r e m 1, it is sufficient to verify that ~ ( 6 ) is compact. Let {(--~}}, c~ E J, be
an a r b i t r a r y net of monothetic subgroups of G. We select f r o m it a subnet {{-'~-fl}}, fi E Jr, that S - c o n v e r g e s to
a certain subgroup X. If all subgroups <x/3 } starting f r o m a certain index are contained in X, then the net
{(-~fi}}, fl E Ji, converges to X in the E-topology also. Otherwise there would exist a subnet {(-~T}}, ~/ E J2,
such that no subgroup <x~/> is contained in X. Since G is c r a m p e d and the net {(--xT)}, ~/ E J2, S - c o n v e r g e s to
X, we can find a To E J2 such that (x~) ~(x~0 ) for all ~/ > ~/0. Since S-convergence is equivalent to convergence
in the E-topology in the lattice ~((x~0)) of the c o m p a c t group <x~/0}, the net ~{~T}}' T E J2, converges to X in
the E-topology.

           Proof,    This c o r o l l a r y follows from the fact that each locally compact c r a m p e d group can be compactly

     COROLLARY. ~ (6) is compact in the E-topology if and only if G is the extension of a compact group
by means of a pure group.
       Proof.    This c o r o l l a r y follows f r o m the description of an EK-group and Theorem 4.
          A topological group G with the set n} (G) compact in the E-topology is called an ES-group. Since n~ (6)
is closed in ge (6), each E K - g r o u p is an ES-group. Another example of E S - g r o u p s is the Schmidt topological
group, i . e . , a noncompact group, all p r o p e r subgroups of which are compact. M o r e o v e r , it follows f r o m
C o r o l l a r y 2 of L e m m a 2 that each noncompact ES-group contains a Schmidt subgroup. Therefore description
of an ES-group is possible only up to a Schmidt group. Let us recall that Abelian Schmidt groups are exhausted
by Cp~ and Rp.
      THEOREM 5. The following types of groups exhaust the c l a s s of the E S - g r o u p s that do not contain non-
Abelian Schmidt subgroups:
       1) compact groups;
      2) C ~ X . . . X Coy X K, where p~ . . . . .   Pn are different prime n u m b e r s , K is finite   and the o r d e r of K is
